title: The Last Letter
text:
Margaret had kept the envelope in her drawer for thirty years. It was yellow at the edges, and the handwriting had faded to a pale blue. She had never opened it, although she often thought about the man who had written it. Tonight she finally decided to read it.

Inside, she found only a short note and a small silver key. The note said that the key belonged to a house by the sea, and that the house was now hers. Margaret sat quietly for a long time, unsure whether to feel grateful or angry.

questions.text: How long had Margaret kept the envelope in her drawer?

options: A short note and a small silver key
A letter and a gold ring

questions.text: What does Margaret's reaction at the end of the passage suggest?
options: She is certain about what to do
She has mixed feelings about the gift
She has already decided to sell the house
She is bored by the news

questions.text: What can be inferred about the man who wrote the note?
options: He was a complete stranger to Margaret
He had a connection to Margaret's past
He had recently moved to the sea
He had lost his own house

paragraph_translations: Margaret guardava o envelope na gaveta havia trinta anos. Ele estava amarelado nas bordas, e a letra tinha desbotado para um azul pálido. Ela nunca o tinha aberto, embora pensasse com frequência no homem que o havia escrito. Naquela noite, finalmente, decidiu lê-lo.

Dentro, encontrou apenas um bilhete curto e uma pequena chave de prata. O bilhete dizia que a chave pertencia a uma casa à beira-mar, e que a casa agora era dela. Margaret ficou sentada em silêncio por muito tempo, sem saber se devia sentir gratidão ou raiva.
